minor_characters.name: Sir William Beresford
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Tommy’s brusque uncle who reconciles with him and appears at the Savoy supper (Ch 028–029).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He has no bearing on the conspiracy, Brown’s unmasking, or the couples’ endings and functions only as an end‑note comic reconciliation.

minor_characters.name: Archdeacon Cowley
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Tuppence’s father, mentioned earlier and then wheeled on as a nervous guest at the Savoy supper (Ch 028).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His cameo does not affect the investigation, the Jane Finn plot, or the romances and can be omitted without loss.

minor_characters.name: American Ambassador
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A cordial diner at the Savoy who invites Jane to the Embassy and adds ceremony to the toasts (Ch 028).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He contributes ceremony only; the plot, reveals, and outcomes proceed identically without him.

minor_characters.name: Inspector Japp
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly name‑checked when Hersheimmer learns ‘Inspector Brown’ was an impostor (Ch 006).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The point (that no such inspector exists) can be conveyed as a generic Scotland Yard denial without using a named character.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Sweeny
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Ebury village key‑holder next to the post office who lends the Moat House key (Ch 021).
minor_characters.reason_removable: She facilitates a door but adds no plot information; the key exchange can be elided in a tighter transition to the empty house.

minor_characters.name: Henry (Ritz page‑boy)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Page who reports Tuppence’s hasty departure for the wrong station and the crumpled telegram (Ch 019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His function (alerting Julius/Tommy to the fake summons) can be folded into Julius finding the note or desk copy without adding a new character.

minor_characters.name: Annie (Mrs. Vandemeyer’s departing maid)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One‑scene servant who grumbles about Mrs. Vandemeyer and is replaced by Tuppence (Ch 010).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Tuppence’s undercover entry can proceed via a direct interview with Mrs. Vandemeyer without Annie’s interlude.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Edgar Keith
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One of several names visited during the ‘Lusitania survivors’ canvass (Ch 007).
minor_characters.reason_removable: A visited name that yields nothing; trimming these dead‑end stops keeps the ‘Rita Vandemeyer’ lead and loses no plot.

minor_characters.name: Miss Wheeler
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Lady’s maid address on the survivors list that the duo considers and discards (Ch 007).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Another fruitless stop that can be cut while preserving the search’s payoff (identifying ‘Rita’ as Marguerite Vandemeyer).

minor_characters.name: Dr. Roylance
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Sir James’s medical friend who houses the concussed Jane in Manchester (Ch 020).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Jane’s temporary lodging can remain unnamed (‘Sir James’s doctor friend’) without a named introduction.

minor_characters.name: George (Julius’s chauffeur)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Naval man who drives Julius to Gatehouse and the staged ‘rescue’ (Ch 024–025).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His presence is incidental; the car and Julius suffice for the ambush/rescue beat.

subplots.name: Savoy supper party and formal toasts (with diary recap and dignitary cameos)
subplots.reason_removable: This epilogue restates solved mysteries and adds social colour; the plot has culminated at Soho and the romances can resolve without the banquet scene.

subplots.name: Tommy’s inheritance and reconciliation with his uncle
subplots.reason_removable: The sudden ‘home and allowance’ coda does not influence the conspiracy, Brown’s fall, or the couples’ decisions.

subplots.name: Julius proposes to Tuppence (comic triangle feint)
subplots.reason_removable: A light diversion that neither alters Julius’s end‑match with Jane nor Tommy and Tuppence’s arc; removing it tightens the middle.

subplots.name: Julius’s Hollywood-style plan to recreate a shipwreck to cure amnesia
subplots.reason_removable: A fanciful brainstorm that is never attempted and adds no causal steps to finding Jane.

subplots.name: Door‑to‑door ‘Lusitania survivors’ canvass montage
subplots.reason_removable: Most waypoints (e.g., Keith, Wheeler) are dead ends; the sequence can be compressed to the single payoff—spotting ‘Rita’ as Marguerite Vandemeyer—without listing fruitless calls.

digressions.topic: Sir James reads Mr. Brown’s diary—an essayistic manifesto on crime, power and method
digressions.reason_removable: This psychological apologia is interesting but nonessential; Brown’s identity, death, and plot are already settled.

digressions.topic: Dr. Hall’s amnesia disquisition (case parallels) and Julius’s speculative ‘hire a liner’ cure
digressions.reason_removable: The long aside explains amnesia mechanics but the story proceeds identically once Jane is found and her memory later returns at Soho.
